newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Leading Slovak shares quiet, SAX edges higher.
newsitem.headline: Leading Slovak shares quiet, SAX edges higher.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were steady in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with gains to shares of drug maker Slovakofarma pushing the SAX index up 0.24 points to 206.84 points.
Slovakofarma firmed 100 crowns to 5,200, while bank VUB closed up 18 crowns at 1,700, to push the market higher, though dealers cautioned volumes were too small to determine any real market trend.

"The market is in an inert mood at the moment, with a lack of reasonable offer or demand," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said. "Investors are likely awaiting the results of annual shareholders' meetings in most of companies, which are expected soon."

Steel maker VSZ closed down five crowns at 710, but Sykora said he expected the issue to show further losses in next week. "VSZ seems returning to its normal cyclic life, after last week's, 350,000 share direct deal," he said.
Overall volume plunged to 334,101 shares, from 1,975,782 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover fell to 221.4 million crowns from 1.089 billion.
